results.title: Nil left ideal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A left ideal $I$ of a ring $R$ is nil if each of its elements is nilpotent: for every $x \in I$ there is a natural number $n$ with $x^n = 0$.

results.title: Köthe's conjecture
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every ring $R$ (associative, with identity) and all nil left ideals $I$ and $J$ of $R$, the sum $I + J$ is again a nil left ideal.

results.title: Köthe's conjecture is false
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a ring $R$ (associative, with identity) and nil left ideals $I$ and $J$ of $R$ (left ideals all of whose elements are nilpotent) such that the sum $I + J$ is not nil.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 15.5 (statement): infinite finitely generated simple amenable groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there exists a group $G$ that is infinite, finitely generated, simple and amenable, where amenable means that $G$ satisfies the Følner condition.

results.title: Juschenko–Monod theorem (Kourovka Problem 15.5)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exists a group $G$ that is infinite, finitely generated, simple and amenable, where amenable means that $G$ satisfies the Følner condition.

results.title: Kourovka 14.62: a maximal soluble subgroup whose normalizer supplements
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every finite group $G$ and every non-soluble normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ there is a maximal soluble subgroup $S$ of $H$ (a soluble subgroup $S \le H$ contained in no strictly larger soluble subgroup of $H$) such that $G = H\,N_G(S)$, where $N_G(S)$ is the normalizer of $S$ in $G$; since $H$ is normal, this says that $H$ and $N_G(S)$ generate $G$.

results.title: Zenkov–Monakhov–Revin theorem (Kourovka 14.62)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite group $G$ and every non-soluble normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ there is a maximal soluble subgroup $S$ of $H$ (a soluble subgroup $S \le H$ contained in no strictly larger soluble subgroup of $H$) such that $G = H\,N_G(S)$, where $N_G(S)$ is the normalizer of $S$ in $G$; since $H$ is normal, this says that $H$ and $N_G(S)$ generate $G$.

results.title: Nottingham condition on automorphisms of power series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A ring automorphism $\varphi$ of the power series ring $R[[x]]$ satisfies the Nottingham condition when $\varphi(x) - x$ lies in the ideal generated by $x^2$, that is, when $\varphi(x) = x(1 + a_1 x + a_2 x^2 + \cdots)$ for some $a_1, a_2, \ldots \in R$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 12.24 (free subgroups of the Nottingham group)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every prime $p$ there is an injective group homomorphism from the free group $F_2$ on two generators to the group of ring automorphisms of $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})[[x]]$ whose image consists of automorphisms $\varphi$ with $\varphi(x) - x \in (x^2)$, that is, of elements of the Nottingham group $N(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})$.

results.title: The Nottingham group contains a free subgroup of rank 2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every prime $p$ there is an injective group homomorphism $f$ from the free group $F_2$ on two generators to the group of ring automorphisms of the power series ring $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})[[x]]$ such that, for every $g \in F_2$, the automorphism $\varphi = f(g)$ satisfies $\varphi(x) - x \in (x^2)$; that is, the Nottingham group $N(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})$ contains a copy of $F_2$.

results.title: The relator of Kourovka Problem 18.86

results.title: Kourovka Problem 18.86 (statement)

results.title: The one-relator group of Kourovka Problem 18.86 is linear

results.title: Ray class character
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A ray class character of a modulus $m$ of a number field $K$ is a group homomorphism from the ray class group of $m$ to the unit circle $\{z \in \mathbb C : |z| = 1\}$.

results.title: Trivial character
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The trivial ray class character of a modulus $m$ of a number field $K$ is the ray class character sending every ray class of $m$ to $1$.

results.title: Pullback of a ray class character to ideals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a ray class character $\chi$ of a modulus $m$ of a number field $K$, its pullback is the group homomorphism from the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $m$ to the unit circle sending $\mathfrak a$ to $\chi([\mathfrak a])$, where $[\mathfrak a]$ is the ray class of $\mathfrak a$.

results.title: Pulled-back ray class characters are trivial on the ray group
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\chi$ be a ray class character of a modulus $m$ of a number field $K$. If a nonzero fractional ideal $\mathfrak a$ of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $m$ lies in the ray group of $m$, then the pullback of $\chi$ to the fractional ideals coprime to the finite part of $m$ takes the value $1$ at $\mathfrak a$.

results.title: Complex value of a ray class character
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a ray class character $\chi$ of a modulus $m$ and a ray class $x$ of $m$, the complex value of $\chi$ at $x$ is $\chi(x)$, a point of the unit circle, regarded as a complex number.

results.title: Ray class characters take the complex value $1$ on the ray group
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$ and $\chi$ a ray class character of $m$. If a nonzero fractional ideal $\mathfrak a$ of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $m$ lies in the ray group of $m$, then the value of $\chi$ at the ray class of $\mathfrak a$, regarded as a complex number, is $1$.

results.title: Cyclic letter shift
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $L \in \mathbb{N}$ and letters $a, t$ of the alphabet $\{0, \dots, L-1\}$, the cyclic shift of $a$ by $t$ is the letter $(a + t) \bmod L$. Writing the letters as $a_0, \dots, a_{L-1}$, it sends $a_i$ to $a_{(i + t) \bmod L}$.

results.title: Letters of a cyclically shifted word

Then $b$ occurs in $\sigma_t(w)$ if and only if $b = \sigma_t(a)$ for some letter $a$ occurring in $w$.

results.title: Cyclic shifting preserves word length

results.summary: For every commutative semiring $R$, every $x \in R$ and all coefficients $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1} \in R$, the value returned by Horner evaluation of $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}$ at $x$ equals $p(x)$, where $p = a_0 + a_1 X + \dots + a_{n-1} X^{n-1} \in R[X]$ is the polynomial with these coefficients.

results.title: Horner evaluation of the empty coefficient list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every commutative semiring $R$ and every $x \in R$, Horner evaluation at $x$ with no coefficients ($n = 0$) returns $0$ and charges $0$ operations.

results.title: Horner evaluation of a constant polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every commutative semiring $R$, every $x \in R$ and every single coefficient $a_0 \in R$ ($n = 1$), Horner evaluation of $a_0$ at $x$ returns $a_0$ and charges $2$ operations.

results.title: Horner evaluation at zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every commutative semiring $R$ and all coefficients $a_0, \dots, a_n \in R$ (at least one coefficient), the value returned by Horner evaluation of $a_0, \dots, a_n$ at $x = 0$ is $a_0$.

results.title: Square matrix accumulation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with an addition and a multiplication, and let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $n \times n$ matrices over $\alpha$, stored as vectors of rows. Square matrix accumulation on $A$, $B$, $C$ is rectangular matrix accumulation on $A$, $B$, $C$ with all three dimensions equal to $n$: it adds $AB$ to the accumulator $C$ and returns the result with its cost pair (scalar multiplications, scalar additions).

results.title: Entries of rectangular matrix accumulation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a commutative additive monoid with a multiplication, and let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $p \times q$, $q \times r$ and $p \times r$ matrices over $\alpha$, stored as vectors of rows. For all $i < p$ and $j < r$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the matrix returned by rectangular matrix accumulation on $A$, $B$, $C$ is $C_{ij} + \sum_{k < q} A_{ik} B_{kj}$.

results.title: Rectangular matrix accumulation computes $C + AB$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a commutative additive monoid with a multiplication, and let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $p \times q$, $q \times r$ and $p \times r$ matrices over $\alpha$, stored as vectors of rows. The matrix returned by rectangular matrix accumulation on $A$, $B$, $C$ equals $C + AB$, where $AB$ is the matrix product, $(AB)_{ij} = \sum_{k < q} A_{ik} B_{kj}$.

results.title: Operation count of rectangular matrix accumulation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with an addition and a multiplication, and let $A$, $B$, $C$ be $p \times q$, $q \times r$ and $p \times r$ matrices over $\alpha$. Rectangular matrix accumulation on $A$, $B$, $C$ has cost $(pqr, pqr)$: it charges exactly $pqr$ scalar multiplications and exactly $pqr$ scalar additions.

results.title: Rectangular matrix accumulation with zero inner dimension
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with an addition and a multiplication. If $A$ is a $p \times 0$ matrix, $B$ a $0 \times r$ matrix and $C$ a $p \times r$ matrix over $\alpha$, then rectangular matrix accumulation on $A$, $B$, $C$ returns $C$ unchanged at cost $(0, 0)$.

results.title: Size of the KMP prefix table
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every pattern $p$, the KMP prefix table of $p$ has exactly as many entries as $p$ has symbols, one for each symbol of $p$.

results.title: The KMP prefix table stores the pattern
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Each entry of the Knuth–Morris–Pratt prefix table is a pair consisting of a symbol and a failure length. For every type with a Boolean equality test and every list $p$ over it, the list of first components of the entries of the prefix table built from $p$, read in order, equals $p$.

results.title: KMP returns the first match
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ and $t$ be lists over a type with a lawful boolean equality, and write $|t|$ for the length of $t$. For every natural number $i$, KMP search for $p$ in $t$ returns the offset $i$ if and only if $p$ matches $t$ at $i$ and at no $j < i$, where $p$ matches $t$ at $i$ when $i \le |t|$ and $p$ is a prefix of the list obtained from $t$ by dropping its first $i$ elements.

results.title: KMP finds no match exactly when no offset matches
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $p$ and $t$ over a type with a lawful boolean equality, write $|t|$ for the length of $t$. KMP search for $p$ in $t$ returns no offset if and only if there is no natural number $i$ at which $p$ matches $t$, where $p$ matches $t$ at $i$ when $i \le |t|$ and $p$ is a prefix of the list obtained from $t$ by dropping its first $i$ elements.

results.title: KMP finds no match exactly when the pattern does not occur
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $p$ (the pattern) and $t$ (the text) over a type with a lawful boolean equality, KMP search for $p$ in $t$ returns no offset if and only if $p$ is not a contiguous sublist of $t$, that is, there are no lists $u$, $v$ with $t = u \, p \, v$ (concatenation).

results.title: KMP search agrees with the first-infix split
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ and $t$ be lists over a type with a lawful boolean equality, with $p$ nonempty. Let the first-infix split of $t$ by $p$ be the pair $(u, v)$ with $t = u \, p \, v$ (concatenation) and $u$ as short as possible, or nothing if $p$ does not occur in $t$. Then the value returned by KMP search for $p$ in $t$ is the length of $u$ if the split exists, and no offset otherwise.

results.title: KMP search makes linearly many comparisons
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For any pattern $p$ and text $t$, lists over a type with a boolean equality, KMP search for $p$ in $t$ makes at most $2|p| + 2|t|$ symbol comparisons in total, those made while building the prefix table included, where $|p|$ and $|t|$ are the lengths of $p$ and $t$.
